title: Deterministic Routing vs LLM Numeric Scoring
question: When selecting an execution strategy, does categorical feature extraction followed by deterministic routing produce more stable and auditable decisions than asking an LLM to emit the final numeric score?
hypothesis: A deterministic picker fed by bounded categorical features will produce higher routing consistency, clearer decision traces, and fewer unnecessary high-reasoning routes while retaining semantic flexibility where task classification actually needs it.
principles: LLM interpretation is not execution authority
Prefer categorical bounded outputs over unconstrained numeric judgment
Compose the deciding score or route deterministically
Use the lightest sufficient reasoning strategy
Preserve every routing decision as evidence

variants.name: LLM Final Numeric Score
variants.description: The model sees the task and directly returns a numeric suitability score or final route used as the deciding authority.

variants.name: Categorical Features + Deterministic Picker
variants.description: The model may classify bounded task features when semantic interpretation is needed; deterministic code applies policy and selects the route.

task_fixtures.task_shape: simple factual retrieval from already available context
multi-step engineering analysis with known dependencies
known repeated task with a previously verified workflow

evidence_requirements: input task fixture and normalized task features
raw model output where a model is used
deterministic policy inputs and selected route
repeated-run route results for the same fixture

metrics.description: Fraction of fixtures routed to the independently specified expected route.
Fraction of repeated identical fixtures that produce the same final route.
Fraction of decisions outside the allowed route/policy schema.
Fraction of low-complexity fixtures escalated to a higher reasoning strategy than required.
Time required to reach a routing decision, excluding downstream task execution.

success_criteria: Both variants run against exactly the same versioned fixtures.
No result is labelled VERIFIED from model self-judgment alone.
The deterministic variant records the categorical features and policy rule that produced every route.
Repeated runs are sufficient to measure routing stability rather than relying on one anecdotal example.
Published conclusions report measured results and failure cases rather than claiming the hypothesis in advance.

content_angles: Why an LLM should not be the final numeric judge for enterprise routing
A small deterministic picker can be more useful than a bigger reasoning model
How to separate semantic classification from execution authority
